newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Widen vs bloc for now.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Widen vs bloc for now.

text.p: Australian bond yields widened against the dollar bloc after the Reserve Bank left monetary policy on hold with some analysts having predicted an easing as early as today after this week's subdued inflation data.

However, the market still remains fairly confident of a 50 basis point easing after the RBA board meeting on August 5, and does leave the prospect of differentials tightening back to Thursday's post-wages data lows.
The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yields spread made a strong test of 25 basis points on Thursday, its lowest level since the early 1980s.

"We see it at least getting to 25 basis points (again). If the market starts to price in another cut after this one it could go even lower," said David Bassanese, senior economist at Bankers Trust Australia.
However, "We think we are pretty close to the end of the narrowing in spreads," he added.
